name: gizza-ai/time-series-generator
summary: Generate deterministic synthetic time-series data with trend, seasonality and noise

tool.description: Generate synthetic time-series data for tests, demos and examples. The tool builds a timestamp index from start, interval and count; layers configurable trend, seasonality, seeded noise, missing values and outliers; supports one or more parallel series; clamps and rounds values; and returns CSV, TSV, JSON, NDJSON or a stats summary. Randomness is deterministic from seed so the same settings reproduce exactly across chat, CLI and browser. Runs locally and does not upload data.

amplitude.description: Seasonal amplitude. May be a comma-separated list matching period; in multiplicative mode values are fractions of the level, otherwise they are additive units. Default 10.

base.description: Starting level of the series before trend, seasonality and noise are applied. Default 100.

combine.description: How trend and seasonal/noise layers combine. additive sums units; multiplicative treats amplitude and noise_level as fractions of the current level. Default additive.

count.description: Rows to generate, 1-100000. The total count x series is capped at 200000 emitted values. Default 100.

decimals.description: Digits after the decimal point, 0-10. Use 0 for integer-like counts. Default 2.

header.description: Include the timestamp/value header row in csv and tsv output. Ignored by json, ndjson and stats. Default true.

interval.description: Step between rows. Use a positive number plus unit: ms, s, m, h, d, w, mo, q or y, for example 15m, 1h, 1d or 1mo. Calendar months/quarters/years keep month ends aligned. Default 1d.

labels.description: Optional comma-separated labels for value columns. Supply one label per series; leave blank to use value, value_2 and so on.

max_value.description: Optional numeric upper clamp applied after outliers. Leave blank for no upper bound.

min_value.description: Optional numeric lower clamp applied after outliers. Leave blank for no lower bound.

missing_rate.description: Probability that each generated value is blank/null, from 0 to 1. CSV/TSV emit an empty cell; JSON/NDJSON emit null. Default 0.

noise.description: Noise process. gaussian draws normal noise, uniform draws in +/- noise_level, and ar1 creates autocorrelated noise controlled by noise_phi. Default gaussian.

noise_level.description: Noise scale. For gaussian it is the standard deviation, for uniform it is the half-width, and for multiplicative mode it is a fraction of the level. Default 5.

noise_phi.description: AR(1) correlation coefficient used only when noise=ar1. Must be between -0.99 and 0.99. Default 0.7.

outlier_direction.description: Allowed outlier direction: both, up only, or down only. Default both.

outlier_magnitude.description: Outlier size as a multiple of the value: 3 means upward outliers become value*(1+3), downward outliers become value/(1+3). Default 3.

outlier_rate.description: Probability that each generated value receives an outlier multiplier, from 0 to 1. Default 0.

output.description: Result format. csv/tsv emit rows, json emits one object with rows, ndjson emits one object per row, and stats reports achieved min/max/mean/sd plus missing/outlier counts. Default csv.

period.description: Cycle length in rows. Comma-separated lists superimpose multiple cycles, such as period='24,168' for daily and weekly hourly data. Default 7.

seasonality.description: Seasonality shape. Cyclic shapes use period and amplitude; weekday uses weekday_pattern as Monday through Sunday multipliers. Default sine.

seed.description: Seed for the deterministic SplitMix64 random streams. The same settings and seed return identical output in chat, CLI and page. Default 42.

series.description: Number of parallel value columns, 1-20. Columns share the trend/seasonal signal but have independent seeded noise, missingness and outliers. Default 1.

start.description: First timestamp. Accepts YYYY-MM-DD, RFC3339/ISO datetimes, or a Unix epoch seconds value. Default 2024-01-01.

timestamp_format.description: Timestamp output format. auto uses dates for day-or-larger intervals and ISO datetimes for sub-day intervals; epoch emits seconds; index emits row numbers. Default auto.

trend.description: Trend layer. none keeps the base flat; linear adds trend_strength per step; exponential compounds by trend_strength percent per step; logistic makes an S-curve across the requested count; random-walk adds seeded increments. Default linear.

trend_strength.description: Trend amount. For linear/random-walk it is units per step, for exponential it is percent per step, and for logistic it is the total rise from first to last row. Default 0.5.

weekday_pattern.description: Seven Monday-through-Sunday values used when seasonality=weekday. The pattern is mean-centred and scaled by amplitude so it works with additive or multiplicative combine modes.
